Fervo Energy.why: Develops enhanced geothermal (EGS) firm baseload power sold under long-term PPAs; about half of its capacity negotiations are with hyperscalers, so data-center power demand drives its contracted backlog.
Fervo Energy.evidence: CEO: 'approximately 35% of our future capacity negotiations are with utility buyers, 50% are with hyperscalers, and 15% are with non-hyperscaler industrial customers'; 'Our current total of 658 megawatts of signed binding PPAs with $7.2 billion of revenue backlog is evidence of that demand.'

players.product: Enhanced geothermal (EGS) 24/7 baseload power from modular GeoBlocks (Cape Station geocluster, Utah) under long-term PPAs with hyperscalers, utilities and industrial buyers, grid-connected and behind-the-meter

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted backlog $7.2 billion at quarter end, representing 658 megawatts of signed binding PPAs. Beyond that, 'gigawatts of demand at various stages of RFP, term sheet, and contract negotiations'; CEO Tim Latimer: approximately 35% of future capacity negotiations are with utility buyers, 50% with hyperscalers and 15% with non-hyperscaler industrial customers. CFO David Ulrey: pricing in current commercial negotiations is consistent with before, 'a range of pricing from $100-$130 a megawatt hour'. The company discloses PPAs only once signed and binding; on behind-the-meter, 'we're optimistic that we'll have an announcement before year end.'
quarterly_data.figure: $7.2 billion contracted backlog; 658 MW signed binding PPAs; hyperscalers ~50% of capacity negotiations; PPA pricing $100-$130 per MWh

quarterly_data.signal: Cape Phase I (approximately 100 MW, three 33 MW GeoBlocks, fully contracted under two PPAs) is in late-stage commissioning: mechanical completion achieved on GeoBlocks 1 and 2, GeoBlock 3 expected over the next several months; the first wells are connected to the power plant and spinning the turbines. Targeting first power from GeoBlock 1 in Q4 2026 (full power towards the end of Q4) and power from GeoBlocks 2 and 3 by early 2027. CFO: remaining steps include substation work, grid synchronization with several grid counterparties and hot commissioning; 'we still feel like we are on track.'
quarterly_data.figure: Cape Phase I ~100 MW; first power from GeoBlock 1 in Q4 2026; GeoBlocks 2 and 3 by early 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CFO outlook: 'for 2027, we currently anticipate generating between $60 million and $80 million of revenue. This is not our formal revenue guidance'; the wide range reflects possible transmission curtailment in 2027 when the transmission operator brings another asset onto the line from Cape Station to end customers, which management believes is unique to 2027 and unrelated to Fervo's production. CFO: third-party analysts anticipate a mid-single digit amount of revenue in Q4 2026, 'and we continue to believe this is achievable.' Installed-capacity target raised to 1.1 gigawatts by the end of 2030 from 1 gigawatt. Capital expenditures expected to total approximately $850 million-$900 million in the second half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2027 revenue $60 million-$80 million (not formal guidance); 1.1 gigawatts installed by end of 2030 (from 1 gigawatt); 2H 2026 capex $850 million-$900 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 (pre-revenue): operating loss $28.7 million, driven by G&A expenses of $27.4 million; net loss $55.9 million. Capital expenditures $226.5 million versus $108 million a year earlier, reflecting construction at Cape Station and drilling and procurement for the next wave of GeoBlock deployment in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 operating loss $28.7 million; net loss $55.9 million; capex $226.5 million (vs $108 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline: eight GeoBlocks representing 400 megawatts moved from early into advanced development (interconnection queue applications submitted, geological surveys completed, appraisal-well permits secured); 10.5 gigawatts across two geoclusters moved from land holdings into early development after DeGolyer and MacNaughton heat-in-place studies; geothermal mineral rights expanded to over 650,000 acres. Cape Station: 500 megawatts under construction of over 4 GW of total resource potential. Appraisal drilling program begins in Q4, mainly Nevada prospects.
quarterly_data.figure: 400 MW (eight GeoBlocks) to advanced development; 10.5 gigawatts to early development; over 650,000 acres

quarterly_data.signal: Cape Phase II: eight 50-megawatt GeoBlocks with startup planned for 2028, using the Fervo 3.0 well design (7,500-foot laterals, 8 and 5/8 inch casing, average 430 degrees Fahrenheit versus roughly 400 degrees for Phase I); CEO expects approximately 27% more power at Cape 2 than Cape 1 for roughly the same surface capex and an all-in cost of $5,500 per kilowatt, with the long-term target of $3,000 per kilowatt 'still firmly in view'. The Sawtooth 7 well (ninth Fervo 3.0 well) reached nearly 19,500 feet at 460 degrees Fahrenheit in 21 days spud to total depth. A third Helmerich & Payne rig was added at Cape Station; up to 80 wells in the Phase II program, with about 10% fully drilled.
quarterly_data.figure: Phase II eight 50 MW GeoBlocks, startup 2028; ~27% more power per surface capex; all-in cost $5,500 per kilowatt (long-term $3,000)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: 'Our supply chain is really robust, both from an oilfield service and equipment perspective, but also the Organic Rankine Cycle turbines that we utilize. The electrical side of things is no secret in the market, is a little bit more stressed', 'That is where we are using some of this incremental capital to make sure that we have that equipment on time for when we need it.' CEO: no labor challenges foreseen on the drilling side; 'a little bit more pressure' on power plant construction labor, which competes with other generation and data center build-outs.
quarterly_data.figure: electrical equipment 'a little bit more stressed'; ORC turbine and drilling supply robust

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on behind-the-meter data-center supply: GeoBlocks let an initial phase be sited behind the meter and scaled alongside a customer's data center build-out, with construction expected to run concurrently with the data center; 100% of geoclusters still carry a long-term grid-interconnection plan. CFO: in the structures being pursued, Fervo delivers firm geothermal power to the customer's private network while the customer procures the extra generation and storage for its reliability target, so incremental costs are not expected to materially affect project returns. CEO: 'if offtakers need clean, firm power before 2030, Fervo will likely be one of, if not the only way to get it.'
